ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Computational Science
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Nature Computational Science is a multidisciplinary journal that focuses on the development and use of computational techniques and mathematical models, as well as their application to address complex problems across a range of scientific disciplines. The journal publishes both fundamental and applied research, from groundbreaking algorithms, tools and frameworks that notably help to advance scientific research, to methodologies that use computing capabilities in novel ways to find new insights and solve challenging real-world problems. By doing so, the journal creates a unique environment to bring together different disciplines to discuss the latest advances in computational science.   Disciplines covered by Nature Computational Science include, but are not limited to:
  • Bioinformatics
  • Cheminformatics
  • Geoinformatics
  • Climate Modeling and Simulation
  • Computational Physics and Cosmology
  • Applied Math
  • Materials Science
  • Urban Science and Technology
  • Scientific Computing
  • Methods, Tools and Platforms for Computational Science
  • Visualization and Virtual Reality for Computational Science
Nature Computational Science is committed to publishing significant, high-quality research through a fair and rigorous peer-review process that is overseen by a team of full-time professional editors.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Intuitive enzyme design with LLM agents
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01052-3

A collaborative system of large language model agents brings protein engineering closer to natural-language interaction, lowering the barrier between human intent and biomolecular design.
ns1:item.dc:title: Intuitive enzyme design with LLM agents
ns1:item.dc:creator: Terra Sztain
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Computational Science, Published online: 2026-09-22; | doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01052-3

ns1:item.ns1:title: Computational active materials and embodied intelligence in extreme conditions
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01051-4

Embodied intelligence has enabled machines to act autonomously, yet intelligence remains largely confined to digital models, leaving robotic bodies as passive executors. In extreme environments, such as the human brain, where tissues are mechanically and thermally sensitive, conventional electronics can become limiting. Here, we discuss how active materials, which embed intelligence directly within their structure, can expand robotic capabilities in these settings, with a particular focus on the role of computation-aided design.
ns1:item.dc:title: Computational active materials and embodied intelligence in extreme conditions
ns1:item.dc:creator: Yifan Yang
Fan Xu
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Computational Science, Published online: 2026-09-22; | doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01051-4

ns1:item.ns1:title: Reproducibility in the era of large language models
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01061-2

Reproducibility has long been a concern in machine learning research. The rise of large language models adds new layers of complexity, underscoring the need for clearer reporting standards and community-wide best practices.
ns1:item.dc:title: Reproducibility in the era of large language models
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Computational Science, Published online: 2026-09-22; | doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01061-2
